conclusions: The actor gate has one actual caller waiter. Gate entry is committed before resume and is remembered; early navigation termination stores the original error (unexpected success becomes an explicit fixture error). Actor operations have no suspension between checking/storing/taking continuation, so registration-before/after-terminal is covered and the same continuation is not taken twice.

The /held request and navigation terminal result arbitrate under the same lock. Request arrival wins only when actually recorded; otherwise the original terminal error is stored and all matching waiters are removed before resumption. Request callback, terminal callback and stop take the same waiter list, preventing duplicate resume.

Existing production WebViewNavigationWait cancellation resumes the old navigation independently of the suspended afterCommit callback. Awaiting old/new task results does not require the actor hold to be released by those tasks. MainActor awaits permit reentrancy for cancellation and pool callbacks.

On thrown setup/wait/navigation errors, the candidate cancels and awaits the actual owned navigation task and releases the injected hold; server defer cancels its owned connections and drains existing request waiters. No catch-to-success, timeout extension, fake callback, retry or skip is added.

Both failOldDecision branches, the 60-second allowance, two20-second navigation deadlines, original body/nonempty/request-sequence/peak-pool assertions, other test bodies, original response-decision once subcase and real HTTP payloads are byte preserved.
